_doc_2026_09_02: RAISED 9000 -> 12000; timeout_minutes 160 -> 220. The 2026-09-01 'leave 9000 until ONE run of THIS scenario reaches completed' condition above is DISCHARGED BY MEASUREMENT, not by another estimate. Full-matrix run 33590213252 terminal-failed this scenario with `StageTimeoutError: stage 'website_redesign.wait': all 8 attempts timed out` -- but html_render_service.redesign_jobs shows the abandoned job 01a060f2-eb9d-724d-a49b-f76294cf447d COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY at 10:52:09, ~25 min AFTER the orchestrator gave up: 5180s of execution against a 4720s single-attempt wait ceiling. Four other 2-variant jobs the same day executed 5580 / 5885 / 7102 / 7370s, all clean with an empty error_message. So this scenario was never over-budget for a mystery reason -- the orchestrator was quitting on healthy work and then paying for a SECOND render. The structural fix (stages/shared/design_job_stash.py) makes a resumed attempt RE-ATTACH to the same job, so the resume ladder now COMPOSES coverage instead of restarting it. ARITHMETIC: the redesign stage is bounded per attempt at 7200s (blueprints/website_review.py) and its total coverage is bounded by html_render's REDESIGN_MAX_JOB_LIFETIME_SECONDS (9000s after gitops #3319 -- which merges FIRST), because the service ages the job out at 9000s and the re-attached poll then fails loudly with the service's own error. So the worst case this scenario must fit is 9000s of redesign + the critique / script / record / compile stages around it; 12000 gives those ~3000s, and stays below pipeline.run_deadline_seconds (14400) as test_no_scenario_waits_longer_than_the_run_itself_may_live requires. timeout_minutes 220 (13200s) keeps timeout_minutes*60 above deadline + 180 (run-e2e-job.sh's poll window) as test_the_e2e_timeout_ladder_stays_ordered requires. NOT a per-scenario deadline chosen to cure a red: it is derived from the service-side job lifetime, which is the only ceiling that now decides the outcome.
label: website-review-variants
